summary.headline: Orient Technologies Q2 FY27 revenue rose 8.84% QoQ to Rs 219.77 crore while EBITDA margin expanded to 7.57%, driven by services mix.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached Rs 219.77 crore in Q2 FY27, up 8.84% QoQ, with services revenue up 24.95% QoQ to Rs 130.99 crore while product revenue fell to Rs 88.78 crore from Rs 97.09 crore. EBITDA rose 45.6% QoQ to Rs 22.45 crore, though the margin is stated as 7.57% against the 10.20% figure quoted for Q1 (the call also describes margin as "about 10%" and as having expanded 263 bps, which are internally inconsistent with the stated figures). PAT rose to Rs 11.72 crore from Rs 5.17 crore. Management attributed the shift to managed services amid infrastructure product delivery delays and cost increases; H1 revenue was down about 14% YoY, which management attributed to infrastructure weakness.

financial_highlights.change: Stated as +263 bps from 10.20% in Q1; figures as quoted are inconsistent (see overview)
Down from Rs 97.09 crore in Q1
H1 revenue down ~14% YoY per analyst question; management confirmed dip
Rs 132 crore products, Rs 199 crore services; expected to be built by Mar 31, 2027

segments.name: Services (managed services, incl. DaaS, cloud, cyber)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 130.99 crore in Q2, up 24.95% QoQ, now 59.6% of revenue. Order book services component Rs 199 crore; management cites managed services contracts typically 3-year, some 5 to 7 years.

segments.name: Products (infrastructure)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 88.78 crore, down from Rs 97.09 crore QoQ. Order book Rs 132 crore. Management cites delivery delays, rising prices and customer preference for Opex over Capex.

segments.name: Vertical mix (Q2 revenue share)
segments.commentary: ITS 29.1%, Mid-Market and Others 39.2%, BFSI 19.15%, Government and PSU 10.79%, Telecommunications 1.76%.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give forward-looking numbers; said FY27 vs FY26 comparison could not be commented on, but expects sequential growth to continue in Q3 and Q4.
Expects infrastructure product challenges (delivery delays, price increases) to persist for about another year; OEM supply delays may continue to 2028 per industry feedback.
Strategy remains focused on managed services; said margins are sustainable if the approximate 60% services / 40% products mix holds.
Target of being debt-free by March 2027 (company already described as debt-free).
Expects SOC/NOC capacity utilisation to reach full capacity by calendar year 2027.
capex_capacity: Securonix deal: planned investment of about USD 5 million in cybersecurity expansion, hiring around 100 cybersecurity professionals, targeting 12% expansion in cybersecurity customer base.

SOC and NOC facility at Turbhe (Navi Mumbai), funded from IPO proceeds, commercialised only recently; utilisation is in the 'just over double-digit percentage' range, expected to rise quarterly and reach full capacity by CY2027.
OEM lead times now 16 to 18 weeks (around 4 months), making quarter-end billing of new orders difficult.
NPCI server order (Rs 76.20 crore excl. GST, 7-year warranty, 18-week execution) received July 2026; management says delivery is on schedule with delivery expected around the following week.
demand_pricing: Customers shifting to Opex over Capex; management is being selective on infrastructure deals and not chasing volume as aggressively as H1 FY26.
Infrastructure hardware prices rising every week, per management.
Securonix: 3-year contract worth USD 3.15 million; Orient became exclusive value-added distributor and joint go-to-market partner in India.
AWS Managed Service Provider recognition is being used to win larger cloud managed services contracts; Ravindra Malpute is Head of Cloud Solutions and AWS Brand Ambassador.
DaaS customers are credit-screened before offering; management says DaaS numbers are rising QoQ, but gave no revenue figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the strong services contribution and how will it build?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said infrastructure product challenges led to a strategy shift toward managed services (data centre, cloud, cyber, infra management, digital transformation). Services revenue rose from Rs 88.78 crore to Rs 130.99 crore QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins look over the next 2 to 3 years as managed services grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward numbers, saying only that the managed services strategy will remain constant.

qa_highlights.question: What working capital steps are planned and how will they support cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is debt-free and targets remaining debt-free by March 2027; working capital focus is DaaS, where customers are being chosen selectively and screened by a credit agency.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H1 FY27 revenue fall about 14% YoY, and will FY27 exceed FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to infrastructure business challenges and reduced aggressive pursuit of deals; said it would not comment on FY27 vs FY26 but expects QoQ growth to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Services versus products split of the Rs 331 crore order book and average services tenure?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book: Rs 132 crore products and Rs 199 crore services as of Sep 30, 2026. Most managed services contracts are 3-year, with some 5 and 7-year contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Can the NPCI order be delivered on time and how will billing spread across Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: NPCI order was picked up in July with an 18-week schedule and management says it is on track, with no delay or penalty expected. OEM lead times of 16 to 18 weeks make supply of late-quarter orders hard to commit.

risks_watch: Infrastructure product revenue is declining (Rs 97.09 crore to Rs 88.78 crore QoQ; H1 revenue down about 14% YoY) and the order book is only 40% products.
OEM lead times of 16 to 18 weeks and rising hardware prices may limit product billing in Q3 and Q4.
Services margin gains depend on the services mix holding near 60%; a large product order could shift the mix.
SOC/NOC utilisation is only in the low double digits; full utilisation by CY2027 is a stated target.
Margin figures are inconsistent across the call (7.57% vs 'about 10%'; 263 bps expansion does not reconcile with 10.20% to 7.57%). Verify against the filed results.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the services and managed services pivot, and upbeat on margin and QoQ growth. Evasive on forward numbers: management repeatedly declined to give FY27 or margin guidance and was vague on DaaS revenue and utilisation.
key_quotes: If you see the revenue from services has been already grew by 25% approximately, sequentially from quarter on quarter.
Managed services will always give a better margin.

So, until and unless this ratio or the mix of business remains the same, meaning approximately 60% of the services and 40% of the products. If the mix remains the same, I think the margins are definitely sustainable.

adds.what: SOC and NOC facility at Turbhe (Navi Mumbai), funded from IPO proceeds; utilisation just over double-digit %, expected to reach full capacity by CY2027
Securonix cybersecurity expansion, planned ~USD 5 million investment, hiring ~100 cybersecurity professionals

growth.why: Management gives no numeric forward revenue guidance and declined to comment on FY27 vs FY26; it expects sequential growth in Q3 and Q4, backed by a Rs 331.61 cr order book (Rs 199 cr services, Rs 132 cr products) and SOC/NOC full capacity by CY2027, while infrastructure product delivery delays persist for about a year.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA rose 45.6% QoQ to Rs 22.45 cr with services at 59.6% of revenue, but management gave no margin numbers and says margins hold only if the ~60/40 services/products mix holds; reported margin figures (7.57% vs 'about 10%') are inconsistent.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: SOC/NOC facility at Turbhe is commercialised with utilisation only in the just-over-double-digit % range, targeted to reach full capacity by CY2027; Securonix expansion (~USD 5 mn, ~100 hires) is planned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects sequential growth to continue in Q3 and Q4, backed by a Rs 331.61 cr order book (Rs 199 cr services, Rs 132 cr products) to be built by Mar 31, 2027, though H1 revenue was down ~14% YoY and product revenue fell to Rs 88.78 cr from Rs 97.09 cr.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation of the new SOC/NOC is low (double-digit %), so a near-term capex announcement is less pressing; the Securonix USD 5 mn investment is already planned but not dated, and debt-free status limits financing need.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numeric forward guidance and declined to comment on FY27 vs FY26; product headwinds (delivery delays, OEM lead times of 16-18 weeks, rising prices) persist for about a year.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Infrastructure product delivery delays and OEM lead times of 16-18 weeks may limit product billing in Q3-Q4, and OEM supply delays may run to 2028; product revenue already fell 8.6% QoQ (Rs 97.09 cr to Rs 88.78 cr).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product launches were discussed; the NPCI server order and Securonix partnership are existing commitments rather than launches.

rows.label: NPCI server order execution (Rs 76.20 cr excl. GST)
rows.why: Received July 2026 with 18-week execution and management says delivery is on schedule, expected around the following week; this supports Q3 product billing despite OEM lead times of 16-18 weeks.

rows.label: Securonix exclusive value-added distributor and GTM partner (USD 3.15 mn, 3-year
rows.why: Orient became exclusive VAD and joint go-to-market partner in India, with a 3-year contract worth USD 3.15 mn and planned ~12% expansion in the cybersecurity customer base.

rows.label: Debt-free status maintained by Mar 2027
rows.why: Company already described as debt-free and targets remaining debt-free by March 2027, with DaaS customers credit-screened to limit receivables risk.

tone.note: Management was confident on the managed services pivot, QoQ growth and debt-free status, but declined to give forward margin, FY27 or DaaS revenue numbers; analysts pushed on the 14% H1 YoY revenue decline, margin reconciliation, OEM delays and the NPCI delivery timeline.
